note: Independent re-audit against RFC 9494 Section 5 ('Implementations MUST NOT enable these procedures by default') after hardening parseLLGRCapValue with llgrFamilyMax = 36 (RFC 5492 1-octet length cap: 36 * 7 = 252 <= 255), !nlrisplit.Supported(f) omission with warning, and refuse-by-default annotations. Both new checks are strictly restrictive (never enable LLGR by default or add unconfigured families), and ipv4/unicast and ipv6/unicast are RIB-supported and well under 36 tuples so neither confounds the tests. All 4 tagged units are unchanged: TestRFC9494_LLGRNotEnabledByDefault verifies configGROnly emits code 64 without code 71 and checks ze-graceful-restart.yang leaf stale-time (mandatory true, no default); TestRFC9494_LLGREnabledByExplicitConfig verifies explicit long-lived > family > ipv4/unicast emits a 7-byte tuple with LLST 3600; TestRFC9494HelperProceduresOffWithoutLocalConfig and TestRFC9494HelperProceduresOnPerConfiguredFamily exercise both JSON and structured OPEN paths via exchangedLLGRLocked. All 4 units carry current revert records (parseLLGRCapValue 317009a6c8051332, exchangedLLGRLocked 70d642601d33a1e0); whole-body panics prove producer dependency only, with semantic scope supplied by healthy assertions and source inspection.
